findings.obs_text: In Neh 13:13 reliable (H0539) stands directly after considered as what the treasurers were counted. WordNet relates the subgroup to this collection through believe; the verse pairs counting with reliability.
In Job 2:3 fast (H2388H) stands fifteen words after considered, in what the Lord says of Job: he still holds fast his integrity.
findings.grounds: He still holds fast his integrity

older.finding: Holding it fast: "I hold fast my righteousness … my heart does not reproach me" (Job 27:6); "He still holds fast his integrity" (Job 2:3).
older.reason: it states how fast works in a person; the fast collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In 1Sa 1:16 anxiety (H7879) stands eight words after regard, in Hannah's reason against being counted worthless: she spoke out of anxiety.
In Job 1:8 and Job 2:3 fears (H3373) stands nine and ten words after considered, describing the one considered: he fears God.
findings.grounds: who fears God and turns away from evil

findings.obs_text: In Job 37:24 fear (H3372H) stands two words before regard, in the clause before it: men fear God, who does not regard the wise in their own conceit.
In Mat 1:20 fear (G5399) stands fourteen words after considered, in what the angel says to the one considering: do not fear.
findings.grounds: do not fear to take Mary as your wife

older.finding: "Do not be afraid", and the ground given each time.
older.reason: it states how fear works in a person; the fear collection owns it

older.finding: Fear in a man's considering, and fear met in a dream.
older.reason: it states how fear works in a person; the fear collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Job 35:13 empty (H7723H) stands three words before regard and describes what God does not regard: an empty cry.
findings.grounds: God does not hear an empty cry

findings.obs_text: In 1Pe 5:12 stand firm (G2476) closes the verse, eleven words after regard, in the exhortation the letter carries.
In 1Sa 25:25 folly (H5039) stands eight words after regard, in the reason Nabal is not to be regarded: folly is with him.
In Pro 17:28 fool (H0191) stands two words before considered as the one counted: the silent fool is counted wise.
findings.grounds: Even a fool who keeps silent

findings.obs_text: In Deu 9:27 remember (H2142) opens the verse, five words before regard: God is asked to remember the fathers and not to regard the people's stubbornness.
findings.grounds: Remember your servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob

findings.obs_text: In Pro 12:10 mercy (H7356B) stands three words after regard, on the other side of the contrast: the mercy of the wicked is cruel.
findings.grounds: the mercy of the wicked is cruel

findings.obs_text: In Deu 33:9 disowned (H5234A) stands three words after regard, in the parallel lines: not regarding father and mother, disowning brothers, ignoring children, for the sake of the word observed.

In Gen 24:22 finished (H3615G, with H1961 and H0834A at the same place) opens the verse, six words before weighing: when the camels have finished drinking, the man brings out the ring of a given weight.
findings.grounds: When the camels had finished drinking

findings.obs_text: In Mat 1:20 holy (G0040G) stands twenty-five words after considered, in the angel's words on what is conceived: from the Holy Spirit.
In Mar 10:42 exercise authority (G2715) stands eight words after considered, in what those considered rulers do.
findings.grounds: their great ones exercise authority over them

findings.obs_text: In Rom 2:26 precepts (G1345) stands five words before regarded, in the condition of the question: the uncircumcised who keeps the precepts is regarded as circumcised.
findings.grounds: keeps the precepts of the law

findings.obs_text: In Ezr 8:29 guard (H8245) opens the verse, three words before weigh: the gifts are guarded until they are weighed before the priests.
findings.grounds: Guard them and keep them until you weigh them

findings.obs_text: In 2Ch 6:19, Job 35:13 and Act 28:22 hear and listening stand near regard: God is asked to regard and to listen, God does not hear nor regard an empty cry, and the leaders wish to hear Paul. WordNet relates the subgroup to this collection through heed, a synonym; the verses set hearing beside regard.
findings.grounds: nor does the Almighty regard it
